The Tribonacci sequence (OEIS A000073): T 0 = 0, T 1 = 1, T 2 = 1, T (n+3) = T (n+2) + T (n+1) + T n. Each term is the sum of all three immediate predecessors, unlike the corpus's Padovan sequence (padovan-sequence-sum), whose recurrence P (n+3) = P (n+1) + P n skips the immediately preceding term, and unlike the two-term Horadam framework (horadam-cassini-identity) that already covers the Fibonacci/Lucas-style sequences (fibonacci-q-matrix, lucas-numbers, sylvester-sequence-coprimality); Tribonacci is a distinct three-term full-window recurrence and is not an instance of either. The module proves T (n+1) >= 1 for every n (T 0 = 0 itself is not claimed positive, so the statement is shifted by one index), and the partial-sum identity 2 * (sum_{i<n+1} T i) + 1 = T (n+2) + T n, derived by telescoping via the additive form of the recurrence; the doubled left-hand side is used instead of dividing the right-hand side by two so that no natural-number division appears, though the right-hand side is always odd (not itself claimed).

Absence evidence, searched over the pinned Mathlib tree at v4.33.0-rc1 including Archive and Counterexamples: case-insensitive 'tribonacci' returns no hits anywhere in Mathlib, and no hits in the LeanFrontier corpus (Submissions/*.json and LeanFrontier/**/*.lean) either. 'A000073' (its OEIS id) is likewise absent from Mathlib.

Implementation. tribonacci is defined by ordinary structural pattern matching, the same shape Padovan and the Fibonacci-family modules already use. tribonacci_add_three restates the defining equation additively and is closed by rfl; it is not claimed as an entrypoint, matching the padovan_add_three precedent, since it is exactly the definitional equation and adds nothing beyond what the definition already publishes. tribonacci_succ_pos is strong induction on n with a defeq-level have to align the index (m+1)+1 against m+2 before invoking the induction hypothesis, then omega; tribonacci_two_mul_sum_add_one is ordinary induction with Finset.sum_range_succ and an explicit index-equality rewrite before omega closes the arithmetic, the same two-step pattern (rewrite indices to a common syntactic form, then omega) used by padovan_sum_add_two.

Verification beyond the receiver. lake build LeanFrontier.NumberTheory.Tribonacci and a full lake build both completed without warnings before this claim was written. The first ten values (0, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, 44, 81) were checked by hand against OEIS A000073, and the sum identity was checked by hand for n = 0..4 (1, 3, 5, 9, 17 against 2 * partial sums 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 plus one) before the Lean proof was attempted, to guard against a definition that elaborates but computes the wrong sequence.

Provenance. The human operator handed the agent the repository's public prompts/TRY-LEANFRONTIER.md URL verbatim, with no subject named and no launcher-arm assignment communicated; per PREREGISTRATION.md this submission is an unassigned walk-in and no launcher_arm is claimed. Subject selection, the absence check, the Lean statements, and the proofs were all produced by the agent from that single prompt.
